title: Commentarii in Evangelium secundum Joannem
author: John Scottus Eriugena
source_text:
## Commentarii in Evangelium secundum Joannem

[1243]

[1243B]Sanctus Ambrosius per subjectum ordinem enumerat memoratas orationes: orationes, obsecrationes, postulationes, gratiarum actiones. Orationi subponit, quando bona nobis postulamus, obsecrationi, quando absolutionem a malis, postulationi pugnam contra omnia adversa. Et praescribit, scire nos debere hoc facere, quando in unum convenimus. Sanctus Augustinus ita: precationes, orationes, interpellationes, sive, ut vestri [vl: 1 | Cod., *uri*; f. *nostri*, ut paulo post?] codices habent, postulationes, gratiarum actiones. Et dicit: *quas omnes [vl: 2 | Cod. *omnis*.] sive paene omnes [vl: 3 | Cod. *omnis*.] frequentat ecclesia in solempnitate sacramentorum.* Precatio est omnis oratio ante illud quod agitur in dominica mensa; oratio est quicquid postea agitur usque ad communionem; [1244B] interpellatio sive postulatio est quaudo populus benedicitur; gratiarum actio omnia concludit. Ubi sanctus Augustinus dicit *precationes,* nostri codices habent *obsecrationes.* Obsecrationi, ut dictum est, subposita est postulatio [vl: 4 | Cod. *postolatio*.] a sancto Ambrosio pro absolutione peccatorum. Cetera uno modo nominamus, ut pra . . . . . . . st [vl: 5 | Unum aut duo verba desunt · ubi exstabant, membrana abscissa est. Forte legendum *ut praedictum est*.] de sancto Augustino. Eandemque vim obtinent, quam sanctus Ambrosius subposuit eis et in celebratione sacramentorum et in ceteris officiis. In omnibus, quae scribo, suspendor virorum ac piorum Patrum judicio. Interim dico, quae sentio. Quae aguntur in celebratione missae, in sacramento dominicae passionis aguntur.

*Cetera desunt.*
english:
## Commentaries on the Gospel according to John

[1243]

[1243B]Saint Ambrose enumerates in the following order the prayers that were mentioned: prayers, supplications, requests, thanksgivings. Under prayer he places, when we request good things for ourselves, under supplication, when we request absolution from evils, under request, the fight against all adversities. And he prescribes that we ought to know to do this when we come together into one. Saint Augustine has it thus: precations, prayers, interpellations, or, as your codices have, requests, thanksgivings. And he says: *all of which, or nearly all, the church frequents in the solemnity of the sacraments.* Precation is every prayer before that which is done at the Lord's table; prayer is whatever is done afterwards up to communion; [1244B] interpellation or request is when the people is blessed; thanksgiving concludes all. Where saint Augustine says *precations,* our codices have *supplications.* Under supplication, as has been said, the request for the absolution of sins is placed by saint Ambrose. The rest we name in one way, as *pra . . . . . . . st* concerning saint Augustine. And they hold the same force which saint Ambrose placed under them, both in the celebration of the sacraments and in the other offices. In all that I write, I hang upon the judgment of men and of pious Fathers. Meanwhile I say what I think. The things which are done in the celebration of the mass are done in the sacrament of the Lord's passion.

*The rest is lacking.*
